description: An introduction to the Holy Qur'an: its meaning, its revelation to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) over about 23 years, the 114 surahs, makki and madani surahs, its role as guidance, the etiquette of reading and its preservation through memorisation (hifdh).

mcq.questionText: The Holy Qur'an was revealed to which Prophet?
mcq.explanation: The Holy Qur'an is the final revealed book, sent down to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as the last and final messenger.

mcq.questionText: How many surahs (chapters) are there in the Holy Qur'an?
mcq.explanation: The Holy Qur'an is made up of 114 surahs, which vary in length from very short to very long.

mcq.questionText: Over approximately how many years was the Holy Qur'an revealed?

options.text: All at once in one night

mcq.explanation: The revelation came gradually over about 23 years, both in Makkah and in Madinah, according to the needs and events of the time.

mcq.questionText: Surahs revealed before the Prophet's migration (Hijrah), mostly in Makkah, are called:
mcq.explanation: Surahs revealed before the Hijrah are known as Makki surahs, while those revealed afterwards are Madani surahs.

mcq.questionText: The word 'Qur'an' is most commonly understood to mean:

options.text: The recitation or that which is read

mcq.explanation: The word Qur'an comes from a root meaning to read or recite, so it means 'the recitation' or 'that which is read'.

mcq.questionText: A person who has memorised the entire Holy Qur'an is called a:
mcq.explanation: A person who memorises the whole Qur'an is called a hafidh, and the act of memorisation is called hifdh.

mcq.questionText: What is the smallest unit or verse of the Holy Qur'an called?
mcq.explanation: Each verse of the Qur'an is called an ayah, and a group of ayahs forms a surah.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is recommended before touching and reading the Holy Qur'an?

options.text: Being in a state of wudu (ablution)

mcq.explanation: It is part of the etiquette of reading the Qur'an to be clean and in a state of wudu, and to handle the Mushaf with respect.

mcq.questionText: The Holy Qur'an describes itself mainly as a:
mcq.explanation: The central role of the Qur'an is to be guidance (huda) for all of mankind, showing the right path in belief and conduct.

mcq.questionText: In which language was the Holy Qur'an revealed?
mcq.explanation: The Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language, and its original Arabic text has been preserved unchanged.

mcq.questionText: Through which angel was the Qur'an brought down to the Prophet (PBUH)?
mcq.explanation: Angel Jibril (Gabriel) was entrusted by Allah to bring the revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

mcq.questionText: Surahs revealed after the Hijrah, mostly in Madinah, often deal with:

options.text: Only the stories of past nations
Laws, social matters and community life
Only the names of the angels

mcq.explanation: Madani surahs often address laws, social rules and the organisation of the Muslim community, while Makki surahs focus more on faith (tawhid) and the Hereafter.

mcq.questionText: What is the written, physical copy of the Holy Qur'an commonly called?
mcq.explanation: The bound, written copy of the Qur'an is known as the Mushaf, which should be handled and stored with respect.

mcq.questionText: How has the Holy Qur'an mainly been preserved in its original form since the time of the Prophet (PBUH)?

options.text: By writing and memorisation (hifdh) by many people
By translating it into many languages
By changing it for each generation

mcq.explanation: The Qur'an has been preserved both in writing and in the hearts of countless huffadh who memorise it word for word in every generation.

mcq.questionText: Which statement about the Holy Qur'an is correct?

options.text: It is the word of the Prophet himself
It is the literal word of Allah revealed to the Prophet (PBUH)
It was written by the angels
It changes from country to country

mcq.explanation: Muslims believe the Qur'an is the literal speech of Allah, revealed through Angel Jibril to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), unchanged everywhere in the world.

fib.questionText: The Holy Qur'an contains a total of _____ surahs.
fib.explanation: The Qur'an is divided into 114 surahs of varying lengths.

fib.questionText: The Qur'an was revealed gradually over a period of about _____ years.
fib.explanation: Revelation lasted roughly 23 years, during the Prophet's time in Makkah and Madinah.

fib.questionText: A single verse of the Holy Qur'an is called an _____.
fib.explanation: An ayah is one verse; many ayahs together make up a surah.

fib.questionText: A person who has memorised the whole Qur'an is known as a _____.
fib.explanation: A hafidh has committed the entire Qur'an to memory through hifdh.

fib.questionText: Surahs revealed before the Hijrah, mainly in Makkah, are called _____ surahs.
fib.explanation: Makki surahs were revealed before the migration to Madinah.

fib.questionText: Surahs revealed after the migration, mainly in Madinah, are called _____ surahs.
fib.explanation: Madani surahs were revealed after the Hijrah and often deal with community and legal matters.

fib.questionText: The Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet (PBUH) through the angel _____.
fib.explanation: Angel Jibril (Gabriel) brought the revelation from Allah to the Prophet.

fib.questionText: The Holy Qur'an was revealed in the _____ language.
fib.explanation: The original text of the Qur'an is in Arabic and remains unchanged.

fib.questionText: The written, physical copy of the Holy Qur'an is called a _____.
fib.explanation: The Mushaf is the bound copy of the Qur'an, handled with respect.

fib.questionText: The main role of the Qur'an is to act as _____ for all mankind.
fib.explanation: The Qur'an is described as guidance (huda) showing people the straight path.

tf.questionText: The Holy Qur'an was revealed all at once in a single moment.
tf.explanation: It was revealed gradually over about 23 years according to events and needs.

tf.questionText: There are 114 surahs in the Holy Qur'an.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an is made up of 114 surahs.

tf.questionText: Makki surahs are those that were revealed after the Prophet migrated to Madinah.
tf.explanation: Makki surahs were revealed before the Hijrah; surahs revealed after it are Madani.

tf.questionText: A person who memorises the entire Qur'an is called a hafidh.
tf.explanation: Such a person is a hafidh, and the memorisation is called hifdh.

tf.questionText: The Holy Qur'an was originally revealed in the Swahili language.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic, not Swahili.

tf.questionText: It is recommended to be in a state of wudu when reading the Holy Qur'an.
tf.explanation: Being clean and in wudu is part of the proper etiquette of reading the Qur'an.

tf.questionText: The Qur'an was brought to the Prophet (PBUH) by the angel Israfil.
tf.explanation: The revelation was brought by the angel Jibril (Gabriel), not Israfil.

tf.questionText: Muslims believe the Holy Qur'an is the literal word of Allah.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an is regarded as the direct speech of Allah, revealed through Jibril.

tf.questionText: The text of the Holy Qur'an changes from one country to another.
tf.explanation: The original Arabic text of the Qur'an is the same everywhere in the world.

tf.questionText: A group of verses together forms a surah.
tf.explanation: Several ayahs (verses) are joined together to make up a surah (chapter).

summary.correctAnswer: It means the recitation or that which is read.
summary.explanation: The name comes from a root meaning to read or recite.

summary.questionText: Number of surahs in the Qur'an
summary.explanation: They range from very short to very long chapters.
Revelation happened in stages in Makkah and Madinah.

summary.correctAnswer: Makki were revealed before the Hijrah, Madani after it.
summary.explanation: The division is based on the time of revelation relative to the migration.

summary.correctAnswer: It is guidance for all mankind.
summary.explanation: It shows the straight path in belief, worship and conduct.
Many ayahs together form a surah.

summary.correctAnswer: Hifdh is memorising the Qur'an; a hafidh is one who has memorised it.
summary.explanation: Memorisation helps preserve the Qur'an in every generation.
Its original Arabic text remains unchanged.

summary.correctAnswer: Be clean and in wudu, and handle the Mushaf with respect.
summary.explanation: Reading calmly and respectfully is part of good adab.

summary.questionText: How the Qur'an has been preserved
summary.correctAnswer: Through writing and memorisation by many people.
summary.explanation: Both the Mushaf and the huffadh keep the text intact.

hoq.questionText: Why is the division of the Qur'an into Makki and Madani surahs useful for understanding its message?

options.text: It tells us the price of each surah
It helps show the context, with Makki surahs focusing on faith and the Hereafter and Madani surahs on laws and community life
It changes the number of verses in the Qur'an
It shows which surahs may be removed

hoq.explanation: Knowing whether a surah is Makki or Madani helps a reader understand the situation it addressed, since early Makkan revelation built faith while Madinan revelation organised the community.

hoq.questionText: Why is the gradual revelation of the Qur'an over about 23 years considered wise rather than a single revelation?

options.text: Because it made the Qur'an shorter
Because gradual revelation made it easier to understand, memorise and apply, and allowed guidance to address real events
Because the angel could only carry a little at a time
Because it reduced the number of surahs needed

hoq.explanation: Step by step revelation helped the believers absorb, memorise and act upon the teachings, and let the guidance respond to the questions and events of the time.

hoq.questionText: How do writing and memorisation (hifdh) work together to keep the Qur'an protected from change?

options.text: Writing replaces the need for any memorisation
Memorisation replaces the need for any written copy
The written Mushaf and the memories of many huffadh check one another, so any error can be corrected
They have no real effect on preservation

hoq.explanation: Because countless people memorise the Qur'an exactly and it is also written down, the two sources confirm each other and protect the text from any alteration.
